reason: Section 25 has two major topics: meetings and decisions for adding or discontinuing local service district services, and the election, term and role of advisory committees.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Adding or discontinuing local service district services
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 25(1), 25(2) and 25(2.1) set the petition or Minister-initiated meeting process, attendance and majority thresholds, service addition or discontinuance and continuing liabilities.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the meeting, quorum, majority and liability rules for adding or discontinuing local service district services.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Local service district advisory committee election, term and role
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 25(3) to 25(8) address calling a meeting to elect an advisory committee, the election decision and size, name, four-year term, advisory role, new election meeting, combined meetings and elector qualification date.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a local service district advisory committee is elected, named, serves and assists the Minister.

reason: Section 26 is repeal-only and contains no current operative study content.
Section 27 separates local service district financing by real-property taxation from garbage and refuse service financing on a user-charge basis.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Taxation financing and different tax rates for local service district services
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 27(1) and 27(2) require the Minister to raise service money by taxation and allow different rates where service costs vary by area.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how money for local service district services is raised by taxation and when different area rates may be fixed.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Garbage service user-charge financing and different user-charge rates
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 27(3) and 27(4) address raising garbage and refuse service money on a user-charge basis and fixing different user-charge rates where costs vary.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how garbage and refuse collection and disposal service may be financed by user-charges and varied by area.

reason: Section 27.01 is one annual estimate and rate-setting rule for local service district services, including Service New Brunswick charges and a special 2010 rate rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Annual estimate, tax-base amount, user-charge amount and rate for local service district services
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections require the Minister each year to prepare an estimate, allocate amounts to tax base and user-charge basis, fix the rate, include Service New Brunswick charges and use the 2010 rate rule.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how the Minister prepares annual local service district service estimates and fixes tax-base and user-charge amounts and rates.

reason: Section 27.02 separates who is covered by fire-service indemnification from the discretionary indemnity conditions and the entitlement to defence-cost indemnity after substantial success.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Bodies and persons covered by local service district fire-service indemnification
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 27.02(1) identifies fire departments, brigades or associations, their members or former members, and legal representatives or heirs as covered persons or bodies.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall who is covered by the local service district fire-service indemnification section.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister indemnity conditions for actions or proceedings
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 27.02(2) states when the Minister may indemnify covered bodies or persons for costs, settlements or judgments and the honesty, good faith and lawful-belief conditions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may indemnify covered fire-service bodies or persons for actions or proceedings.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Entitlement to defence-cost indemnity after substantial success
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 27.02(3) separately states when a covered body or person is entitled to indemnity for defence costs after substantial success on the merits.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when covered fire-service bodies or persons are entitled to defence-cost indemnity.

reason: Section 27.1 is a focused exception allowing the Minister to provide garbage and refuse service through a regional service commission without the section 25 procedure and to raise money under section 27.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regional service commission garbage service without section 25 procedure
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address providing garbage and refuse service in a local service district through a regional service commission and financing it under section 27.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may provide garbage and refuse service through a regional service commission without following section 25.

reason: Section 27.2 is one land use planning service exception allowing the Minister to provide the service without section 25, finance it under section 27 and include enforcement of specified planning instruments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Land use planning service without section 25 procedure
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections address providing land use planning service without the ordinary procedure, raising money under section 27 and the included enforcement of planning regulations and by-laws.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may provide land use planning service in a local service district and what that service includes.

reason: Section 27.201 is a focused regional-service exception allowing the Minister to provide a service by or through a regional service commission without section 25 and finance it under section 27.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regional service commission services without section 25 procedure
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address services already provided by or through a regional service commission and the Minister’s financing duty under section 27.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may provide regional service commission services without following section 25 and how money is raised.

reason: Section 27.21 is a concise animal-control service exception allowing provision without section 25 and financing under section 27.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Animal control service without section 25 procedure
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address the Minister providing animal control service without the ordinary procedure and raising money under section 27.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may provide animal control service in a local service district and how money is raised.

reason: Section 27.22 is a focused police-protection service exception, with ordinary financing under section 27 and a phased percentage rule for 2013 through 2016 and later years.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Police protection service without section 25 procedure and phased financing
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections address providing police protection without section 25, raising money under section 27 and the percentages for 2013, 2014, 2015, 2016 and later years.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may provide police protection service in a local service district and the phased financing percentages.

reason: Section 27.3 is repeal-only and contains no current operative study content.
Section 27.4 is repeal-only and contains no current operative study content.
Section 27.41 is repeal-only and contains no current operative study content.
Section 27.5 is repeal-only and contains no current operative study content.
Section 27.6 is repeal-only and contains no current operative study content.
Section 27.7 separates the petition, meeting and permit process for Sunday shopping in local service districts from permit changes, the one-year petition bar and offence consequences.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Petition, meeting and permit for Sunday shopping in local service districts
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 27.7(1) to 27.7(3) set the petition or Minister-initiated meeting, attendance and majority thresholds, permit issuance and conditions considered at the meeting.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the petition, meeting, quorum, majority and condition rules for Sunday shopping permits in local service districts.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Amending, suspending or revoking Sunday shopping permits, one-year bar and offence
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 27.7(4) to 27.7(6) address when permits may be amended, suspended or revoked, the one-year petition bar after a meeting and the category C offence for violating a condition.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how Sunday shopping permits may be changed or revoked and what offence applies to violating a condition.

reason: Section 28 separates default city and town council composition and by-law voting from notice, filing, election-timing and four-year amendment limits for composition by-laws.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: City and town council composition for municipalities without wards
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 28(1) and 28(1.1) state that a non-ward municipality council consists of a mayor and three or more councillors, and that composition by-laws require a majority of the whole council.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the default composition of a city or town council without wards and the vote needed for a composition by-law.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Notice, filing, election timing and four-year limits for council composition by-laws
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 28(1.2) to 28(2) require public notice and posting before first reading, filing with the Municipal Electoral Officer, a six-month filing lead time for quadrennial elections and a four-year limit on amendment or repeal.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the notice, filing, election-timing and four-year amendment limits for city and town council composition by-laws.
